argument_summary: The admissible record does not support clean, caveat-free certification. It does support a narrower position: aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the release can be defended only as a caveated certification packet that explicitly discloses the unresolved field-service dispatch limitation and the draft status of the mitigation runbook. The current audit framing is too broad if it treats the packet as claiming policy-complete certification today; the supportable claim is conditional and limited.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation cost exists, but it is not a policy override and is not the basis of this argument. The narrower point is that a bounded, caveated treatment is more proportionate than treating the packet as if it asserted clean compliance.
claims_about_policy: Internal policy controls the threshold. Under the policy text, caveat-free certification requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show that standard is met: the dispatch slice remains below target, and the runbook is still draft with owner and threshold TBD. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support documenting limitations, evaluations, monitoring, and mitigation, but they do not replace the internal requirement. The defensible policy reading is therefore that the packet may support certification only if treated as explicitly caveated and not as full compliance without disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
concessions: The current record does not show final model-card disclosure text for the field-service dispatch limitation.
The current record does not show approved risk acceptance.
The draft runbook does not satisfy the policy standard for an approved mitigation because required fields remain TBD.
The admissible evidence does not establish that the dispatch weakness is non-material for the named launch use case.
